rows.requirement: Published artifacts (business profiles, and the schema and transport-description artifacts they reference) MUST be served over HTTPS.
rows.quote: Published artifacts **MUST** be served over HTTPS.
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] REWORDED — flag for review: relocated docs/specification/overview.md -> docs/specification/overview/index.md (doc-tree reorg #723). OLD (04-08, #L1053): 'Profiles **MUST** be served over HTTPS.' NEW (08-25, #L2238): 'Published artifacts **MUST** be served over HTTPS.' Scope broadened: the new '### Profile Requirements / #### Hosting' section explicitly states 'Profiles, and the schema and transport-description artifacts they reference, must be reliably hosted' — so the HTTPS rule now binds every artifact a profile references, not just the profile document itself. Human review: consider extending our HTTPS check to schema/transport-doc fetches, not just the initial profile fetch. Profile is still the business well-known profile document.

rows.requirement: Profile endpoints MUST NOT use 3xx redirects; verifiers MUST NOT follow them.
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] relocated only; wording unchanged (still scoped to 'Profile endpoints', not broadened like DISC-001/003/004). Companion impl rule (verifier-side, now itself broadened) at new #L2287: 'Implementations **MUST NOT** follow redirects (3xx).' — see DISC-004 for the parallel HTTPS broadening on that same verifier-rules list. Browser fetch auto-follows redirects opaquely -> CLI-only to assert no-redirect.

rows.requirement: Published artifact responses MUST send Cache-Control with public and max-age>=60, and MUST NOT use private/no-store/no-cache.
rows.quote:
Published artifacts **MUST** include a `Cache-Control` header with
`public` and `max-age` of at least 60 seconds, and **MUST NOT** be
served with `private`, `no-store`, or `no-cache` directives.
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] REWORDED — flag for review: relocated overview.md -> overview/index.md. OLD (04-08, #L1055-1057): 'Profile responses **MUST** include a `Cache-Control` header with `public` and `max-age` of at least 60 seconds. Profiles **MUST NOT** be served with `private`, `no-store`, or `no-cache` directives.' (two sentences, scoped to profile responses/profiles). NEW (08-25, #L2240-2242): merged into one sentence and re-scoped from 'Profile responses'/'Profiles' to 'Published artifacts' — same broadened-scope change as DISC-001. Also NEW and not previously present: a 4th numbered rule at #L2243-2244 — 'Published artifacts **SHOULD** include a validator (`ETag` or `Last-Modified`) so consumers can revalidate cached copies efficiently.' Out of scope to add as a new row in this carry-forward pass; flagged for a future completeness sweep. Reading response headers cross-origin is CORS-restricted in browser -> CLI-only.

rows.requirement: Implementations MUST reject URLs (the profile, or any jwks_uri / CIMD document dereferenced during identity resolution) not served over HTTPS.
rows.quote: Implementations **MUST** reject URLs not served over HTTPS.
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] REWORDED — flag for review: relocated. OLD (04-08, #L1098): 'Implementations **MUST** reject profile URLs not served over HTTPS.' NEW (08-25, #L2286): 'Implementations **MUST** reject URLs not served over HTTPS.' — dropped the word 'profile'; the immediately preceding sentence (#L2283-2284) explicitly broadens scope: 'These rules apply to any URL dereferenced during identity resolution — the profile, and any `jwks_uri` or CIMD document a verifier follows.' So the HTTPS-only requirement now explicitly covers jwks_uri and CIMD document fetches too, not just the profile URL. Human review: confirm our tester's URL-scheme check runs against every dereferenced URL in the identity-resolution chain, not only the initial profile fetch. Tester-side behavior we also implement in our own profile fetcher.

rows.requirement: service endpoint MUST be a valid HTTPS URL.
rows.quote: `endpoint` **MUST** be a valid URL with scheme (https)
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] relocated only; same '### Services' rules list, wording unchanged, line shifted 147->1035. Official suite protocol_test still asserts a non-null rest endpoint.

rows.requirement: Platforms MUST include their profile URI in every request.
rows.quote:
Platforms **MUST** include their profile URI in
every request using the transport-appropriate mechanism.
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] relocated only (now under '### Negotiation Protocol / #### Platform Requirements', item 1 'Profile Advertisement'); wording unchanged, line shifted 622->1780. Still REST: UCP-Agent header (RFC 8941 dictionary, profile=). This is the platform/agent obligation; the tester IS the platform and must send it — same subject-binding as before (reclassified 2026-07-02, unaffected by this reorg). The tester itself satisfies the obligation as the platform: every suite request carries UCP-Agent profile=... (merchant_checks._hdr).

rows.requirement: Implementations MUST NOT follow redirects (3xx) when dereferencing a URL during identity resolution (the profile, or any jwks_uri / CIMD document a verifier follows).
rows.notes: New row, 2026-08-25 census closure wave. This is the broadened verifier-side no-redirect rule (rule 2 of the URL fetch-safety list) that DISC-002 already flagged as an unregistered companion: DISC-002 covers the narrower, unchanged "Profile endpoints MUST NOT use redirects (3xx)" statement at L2239; this row covers the broadened rule 2 in the fetch-safety list at L2287, which DISC-004 (rule 1, HTTPS-only) already establishes applies to every URL dereferenced during identity resolution, not just the initial profile fetch. CLI-only: browser fetch auto-follows redirects opaquely.

rows.quote:

rows.requirement: If a business profile cannot be fetched (timeout, DNS failure, 5xx) or fails validation (invalid schema, signing keys, signature mismatch), businesses MUST reject the request with an appropriate error and status code.
rows.quote:
If a profile cannot be fetched (timeout, DNS failure, 5xx) or fails
validation (invalid schema, signing keys, signature mismatch),
businesses **MUST** reject the request with an appropriate error and
status code (see [Error Handling](#error-handling)).
rows.notes: New row, 2026-08-25 census closure wave (Fetching, closing paragraph — the terminal error-handling duty when platform-profile fetch/validation fails).
